title: A fast open-source Fiji-macro to quantify virus infection and transfection on single-cell level by fluorescence microscopy
author: Kerkhoff, Wedepohl, et al.

steps.title: Prepare folders and launch macro
steps.instruction: Collect all images to be analysed in a single input folder (subfolders are allowed) and create an empty output folder. Open Fiji, load the provided single‑cell analysis macro and press Run. In the dialog that appears, select the input folder, the output folder, and specify the image file extension without a leading dot (e.g., lif, czi, tif). Indicate which channel contains the nucleus stain and which channel contains the fluorescent marker (other channels will be ignored). Choose analysis parameters: either accept the default values, enter custom values for the background threshold β, segmentation sensitivity ω, and intensity cutoff α (e.g., β = 15, ω = 5, α = 0.4), or request automatic parameter estimation. Confirm to start the analysis. The macro will process each image (≈1–2 s per image on a PC with a 2.5 GHz CPU, 2 cores, 8 GB RAM) and automatically save for every image a segmentation overlay, a log10 intensity histogram, a single‑cell data table (area, mean intensity, x‑y position, circularity, …) and a summary table in the output folder.

substeps.instruction: Gather all images into one input folder (subfolders optional).
Open Fiji and load the macro.
Press Run and set input folder, output folder, and image file extension.
Assign nucleus and marker channel numbers.
Enter or accept analysis parameters (β, ω, α) or enable automatic estimation.
Start the analysis and let the macro write results to the output folder.

steps.title: Validate parameters with control images
steps.instruction: Select at least one control image that contains both fluorescent and non‑fluorescent cells (or two images representing positive and negative controls) and run the macro with the current parameters. Manually inspect the generated segmentation overlay and the log10 intensity histogram for each control image. If the overlay mis‑segments cells or the histogram does not clearly separate fluorescent from non‑fluorescent populations, return to the previous step, adjust β, ω, or α, and re‑run the analysis. Repeat the inspection‑adjustment cycle until the overlays and histograms appear reasonable. Finally, use the summary table (which lists image titles, total cell number, and fluorescent cell number) to calculate the desired metric such as transfection efficiency or infection inhibition.

substeps.instruction: Run the macro on control image(s).
Inspect segmentation overlay and intensity histogram.
If results are unsatisfactory, modify β, ω, or α and re‑run.
Repeat until overlays and histograms are acceptable.
Use the summary table to quantify the property of interest.
